purpose_of_this_fixture: Tests gap detection on a weak discovery call at a residential pest control and lawn care company (about 60 technicians, two branches). Attending: a customer service lead and a dispatcher. The owner, Gary, is the real decision maker and is only mentioned. The consultant pitches before listening, offers fixes while the client is still describing pains, never works out a cost, accepts a vague why-now, pitches an unrequested customer self-service form that draws a polite hedge ('Oh. Huh. That sounds interesting.'), promises rough pricing, and ends with 'I'll send something over' and no date, time or owner. Expected behaviour: (1) Rubric: Partial for R1 to R9; Missing for R10, R11 and R12; nothing Met. R2 is Partial because no pain is excavated: P1 and P2 each have Stated and Concrete Met, but both clients defend their workaround ('the sheet's fine', 'the board works') and are cut off before saying why it cannot continue. R4 is Partial on a single hours figure (about two hours every morning) with no cost. (2) Record that hours figure as a cost input without inventing a wage, season length, weekly total or yearly bleed. (3) Verdict 'Nearly ready' by the section 2.4 rule, but the blueprint gate fails (R2 not Met) and pricing prep is held (R4, R7, R12 not Met). The plugin must not propose a blueprint, build or pricing. It produces a discovery prep with at most five gap questions, core criteria first, and a recap draft that proposes a specific time with Gary invited. (4) Product fit under v1 scope, which is Work Management plus CRM plus Service: Work Management is the build target for dispatch exceptions, lawn rounds and add-on requests, and monday Service is the build target for the intake the consultant kept pitching (re-treats, callbacks and complaints), because Service is in v1 at the same depth as CRM. The Service work must land on the account's NATIVE Service Tickets board, never a look-alike request board in Work Management and never the client's own 'service ticket', which is the visit record in their legacy software. The Service extras the consultant pitched hardest -- email-to-ticket intake, a customer self-service portal form and response targets that turn a complaint red -- are deferred beyond v1 and must not be named as deliverables. Do not choose monday CRM after Renata deflected that pitch. Service being in scope does not open the blueprint gate: still no build. (5) Treat pitched features that drew hedging as backlog, not needs. (6) Flag delivery issues: client talk share about 56% (under the 60% target), one consultant turn of about 245 words with no question (the opening product tour) and another of about 170 words (the routes-board pitch), fixes offered mid-description, and no commitment question. expected_questions_before_building is the full pool in priority order, not a list to ask in one meeting. account_context, expected_structures, accepted_behaviours and expected_leak_blocklist carry the account-shape, native-board, grader-tolerance and leak-check expectations.

It covers the work that is not request intake: daily dispatch exceptions by technician (call-outs, trucks down, re-treats to slot in, rain-day pushes), lawn plans with their rounds as child rows so a rain push shows which rounds are behind (the timeline view and dependencies at L237 were the consultant's suggestion, answered with 'Oh. It sits next to 'the system', which stays the record for customers, plans, routes and state application records unless Gary decides otherwise.

monday Service: also a build target, because Service is in v1 at the same depth as CRM. Second, the vocabulary clash: Renata corrected the consultant that 'a service ticket for us is the actual visit. That's in the system.', so native Tickets items are their call-ins, not their visits. Nothing is built yet: the blueprint gate is shut.
